title: Private: delayed SSO assertions causing audit log gaps and KMS envelope failures
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Multiple enterprise Private customers reported missing audit entries for session events and intermittent KMS envelope decryption failures following recent SSO config changes. Symptoms observed: (1) SAML assertion processing sometimes delays beyond the session creation window, leading to session metadata being written without corresponding audit rows; (2) those partial writes sometimes reference newly provisioned KMS envelopes that the audit worker cannot decrypt, surfacing as KMS_DECRYPT_FAIL in logs. Impact: compliance/audit gaps and elevated error rates for customer-managed KMS integrations.
observed_impact: Several customers reported missing 'session.create' and 'session.bind' audit events during SSO logins
Increased error rate (5xx) from audit-forwarder for affected customers
KMS decrypt failures correlated with timing of SSO assertion processing in the runtime
steps_to_reproduce: Use a Private deployment with customer-managed KMS and SSO (IdP) configured; enable high-latency IdP responses with artificial delay (200-800ms)
Trigger 100 concurrent SSO logins that exercise assertion-to-session flow
Observe the audit DB for missing session events and check audit-forwarder logs for KMS_DECRYPT_FAIL entries
Re-run with assertion processing fast (<50ms) to confirm reduced failures
root_cause_hypothesis: Race between assertion finalization and asynchronous audit write + envelope provisioning. When the assertion callback is delayed, session record is persisted with a placeholder KMS envelope ID. The audit-forwarder consumes events before the KMS envelope is fully rotated/propagated to the worker cluster, causing transient decrypt failures and dropped audit rows.
mitigation_plan: Hotfix: serialize SSO assertion finalization and audit write (short critical section) to guarantee audit events include valid envelope ID before forwarder picks them up
Short-term config: throttle audit-forwarder workers for affected customers to allow envelope propagation (config toggle per-tenant)
Monitoring: add metric to detect audit events with placeholder/missing_kms_id and alert if >0.1% in 5m window

acceptance_criteria: Hotpatch deployed to affected Private clusters with zero rollback incidents
Reproduction harness no longer produces missing audit rows at production-like load (1000 simulated logins) in staging
KMS_DECRYPT_FAIL rate for audit-forwarder drops to baseline (<0.01% across 30m) for impacted tenants
Post-deploy smoke tests validate audit rows exist for every session.create/session.bind event
Security review sign-off attached to PRs and documented mitigation in release notes
rollback_plan: If hotpatch causes increased latency or regressions, revert runtime PR #5173 and immediately flip audit-forwarder throttling to 'safe' mode
Notify affected customers and create a temporary retention export of raw logs for compliance teams
Open follow-up rollback incident with SRE to coordinate cluster-wide revert
postmortem_followups: Implement stronger invariant: audit writes must validate KMS envelope existence before enqueuing forwarder message
Add per-tenant health check in Private console for KMS envelope propagation latency
Create automated chaos tests simulating IdP latency and KMS propagation delays in CI
Document operational playbook for similar SSO/KMS timing issues and train support teams
notes: Trade-offs discussed: full transactional write across session + audit + envelope would be safer but is a larger refactor; hotpatch opts for minimal critical-section serialization to reduce blast radius
We will prioritize a follow-up that removes the placeholder envelope pattern entirely and migrates to explicit envelope provisioning before session persistence
